paragraphs.text: A local voice for your agent: Kokoro-82M on CPU behind a 150-line daemon. ~2.2x real time, first sou
nd under a second, no cloud.
English · 中文 · listen: 16 seconds

**Your agent works for twenty minutes. You are in another window. It tells you what happened — in
it
s own words, in eight seconds.**

This is a narration layer for long agent runs: a local voice daemon, an MCP tool the model calls
whe
n something is worth saying, and a rule for what that sounds like.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why narration
Reading answers aloud is the wrong unit of speech. Long runs are made of milestones, and the person

listening is usually busy: another window, another task, a coffee, a walk around the room. What
they
need is not the reply. It is three things: what just happened, how it went, what comes next.

The words have to be written for that moment. A canned "Task completed successfully" wears out by
th
e third repetition; a line written by the model that did the work sounds like a colleague:

> Tests are green, forty two of forty two. Next I'm taking the API layer.
>
> That type error was mi

ne, the retry path returned the wrong shape. Fixed it, build is clean.
>
> Deploy is live. Nothing i
s on fire, and the last thing left is the changelog.
Those three lines are `docs/demo.mp3`.
## The rule

1. **What I did, how it went, what comes next.** Two sentences, under eight seconds.
2. **Milestones

only** — a batch finished, tests came back, something broke, I am blocked.
3. **Written fresh every

time**, by the model, for that moment. No templates, no status fields read
aloud, no todo list.
4.
**Quiet when nothing changed.** Frequent speech is the point; noise is the failure.

The same rule ships in `skill/SKILL.md`, and the tool description in
`mcp/server.py` repeats it for
agents that never read docs.
## Narrate from an agent

The MCP server exposes `narrate` and `voice_status`. DSH, Claude Desktop, Cursor and anything else
t
hat speaks MCP can use it.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Without MCP, `vox say "..."` does the same thing from a shell.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]

- **Resident daemon.** A cold load costs 3.5 s, so one process keeps the model in memory.
- **Worker

in its own process.** Kokoro needs onnxruntime and espeak-ng; the daemon needs neither.
- **Sentenc

e splitter.** Each sentence is synthesized in turn and handed to the player the moment
it exists, so

the first sound arrives long before the last word.
- **Cache on the sentence.** Repeats cost nothin
g, and the same update never sounds different twice.
## Benchmarks

Measured on a Xeon E5-2673 v3 (Haswell, 24 threads, no GPU), Python 3.14, onnxruntime 1.31.
Reproduc
e with `tools/venv/bin/python tests/bench.py`.

| line | audio | synthesis | speed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| short | 1.71 s | 0.77 s | 2.22× |
| medi
| metric | value |

| median speed | **2.22× real time** |
| model load, cold | 3.55 s |
| first sentence, cold | 0.93 s

|
| first sentence, cached | 0.00 s |
| four-sentence reply | 5.96 s end to end |
| HTTP roundtrip

| ~2 ms |
| disk | 338 MB (311 MB model + 27 MB voices) |

**int8 runs slower on this CPU.** The quantized model took 4.17 s for 4.14 s of audio (1.0×);
fp32 t

ook 1.84 s for 4.22 s (2.3×). Haswell has no AVX-512 VNNI, so int8 matmuls are emulated.
311 MB beat
s 114 MB here, and the table above shows it.
## Using it
[代码示例省略，未执行]
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Design notes

- **The model owns the words.** The daemon renders whatever it is handed, which is why updates
never

repeat a canned phrasing.
- **The cache key is the sentence and the voice.** Same words, same bytes

, zero cost.
- **No framework.** stdlib `http.server`, one subprocess, one thread. 150 lines.
- **Th

e daemon never blocks.** `/say` enqueues and returns in ~2 ms, so an agent turn stalls on
nothing.
## Limitations

- **English voices.** The bundled voice pack is English.
- **2.2× means a four-second sentence costs

about 1.8 s.** Comfortable for updates, slow for
reading a document out loud.
- **Sentence splittin

g can clip prosody** at the joins. Noticeable on literary text.
- **Linux and PipeWire** (`pw-play`)

. Set `VOX_PLAY` to `aplay` or `afplay` elsewhere.
- **espeak-ng data** is required for phonemizatio

n; `install.sh` unpacks it when the system has none.
- **No ears.** `vox listen` needs Underdog Bark
3.0 and torch; not installed by default.
## Credits

- Kokoro-82M — Apache 2.0 weights, by hexgrad.
- kokoro-onnx — ONNX runtime and model exports.
- onn
xruntime, espeak-ng.
